Independent 65-digit mpmath root check of log(2)−log1p(a²)/2+a·atan(a)−(2k+1)πa/3 for k=1,2,3. The k=1 root begins 0.228903469804774575000760; the other two agree at the printed precision.
correctness.rationale: The exact theorem holds. On the orthogonal complement of the constants, J squares to −I, so the exponential has damped cosine and sine entries. The three lower-bound constraints on the scalar exponential are cosines of amplitude 2 centered at π/3, π, and 5π/3 modulo 2π; each dominates on its nearest-center cell. The log difference from aθ is strictly concave there. For a<sqrt(3), its maximum is at cₖ−atan(a) and has height H(a)−acₖ. Positive height gives one open failure interval, zero height a nonnegative tangency, and negative height none. Positive angular cell boundaries separate successive intervals, and the initial time 0 is isolated in the complement. For a≥sqrt(3) the generator is Metzler. Differentiating H(a)/a proves monotone bifurcations and expanding H at 0 gives the count asymptotic. For a real 2×2 matrix the off-diagonal exponential entries are the off-diagonal generator entries times the same scalar divided difference; repeated real eigenvalues give te^(λt), and nonreal eigenvalues give a sine factor that changes sign arbitrarily late. Hence eventual nonnegativity forces a Metzler generator. The displayed a₁ decimal has a minor last-digits error: the exact root is approximately 0.228903469804775, not 0.228903469804832. This does not change the implicit threshold or any theorem.
residual_risks: Approximations are not certified interval enclosures. The proof counts times where at least one entry is negative, not times when the entire matrix is entrywise negative.

originality.rationale: A distinct indexed exact result covers the claimed original staircase, not just eventual positivity. Let C be the directed cyclic permutation, L=I−C, and P the projection onto constants in the frozen record. On ker(P), L has conjugate eigenvalues sqrt(3)exp(±iπ/6) in the same orthogonal rotation plane as J, hence −L^α is −r cos(φ)(I−P) ± r sin(φ)J with r=3^(α/2), φ=πα/6. A transposition or orientation reversal preserves the sign test, and positive time rescaling lets this realize every frozen a=δ/ω=cot(φ)>0 as 0<α<3 varies. The prior indexed window count, endpoints, thresholds, tangencies, and asymptotic are exactly those at issue. The two records' same-day catalogue date does not determine which was found first; it does not remove the verified equivalent coverage. The lower-dimensional rigidity is elementary and the frozen record explicitly does not claim it separately as new.
residual_risks: There is no inference of historical priority from the same-day entries. The rejection rests on directly verified mathematical coverage.
